defect: CONTROL_MANIFEST.sha256 records the pre-freeze GENERATED_UNVERIFIED digest of MODE while the published MODE content is FROZEN. The frozen package therefore fails its own control manifest on exactly one entry.

measured.proof_recorded_digest_is_pre_freeze: sha256 of the exact bytes 'GENERATED_UNVERIFIED\n' equals 0dba1cc2928ed5a2a3259b8d9aa4188feb6b775c91d7eab990bb75fa49cd6eee

regression_origin.r4_outcome: MODE was already FROZEN on disk when the manifest hashed it, so the manifest is self-consistent
regression_origin.r5_outcome: MODE was still GENERATED_UNVERIFIED on disk when the manifest hashed it from disk at controller.py:1239-1240
regression_origin.why_r5_moved_it: publishing MODE last is a real safety property: the package must never visibly claim FROZEN before the other final artefacts exist. R5 gained that property and lost self-consistency.
regression_origin.correct_fix: hash the FINAL-STATE file set from staged bytes, and still publish MODE last. Both properties hold at once. Reverting to the R4 order would restore self-consistency and reintroduce the premature-FROZEN window.

why_no_test_caught_it: No test in R5 executed the real controller freeze route to completion and then verified the produced CONTROL_MANIFEST from disk. automation/package_tests/test_r5_freeze_repair.py exercises the driver's refusals against the live package and asserts that no artefact was written; the success path was never run end to end, so the manifest it produces was never checked.
defect_line_reference: automation/controller.py:1239-1240 (manifest hashed from disk) versus automation/controller.py:1263-1264 (MODE published afterwards)
